content: 1. Administer demeclocycline at a dose of 2 mg/kg/day orally, divided into two or three doses daily (BID/TID). Alternatively, administer 300 mg/m²/day orally, divided into BID/TID doses. 2. Both acitretin and tetracyclines, including demeclocycline, can increase intracranial pressure. These combinations are contraindicated. 3. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the absorption of demeclocycline in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract, leading to decreased drug levels. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or separate administration by at least 2 hours. 4. Aminolevulinic acid (oral) and demeclocycline can increase each other’s toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Additionally, avoid administering other phototoxic drugs with aminolevulinic acid during the perioperative period (24 hours). 5. Demeclocycline increases the toxicity of aminolevulinic acid (topical) via pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 6. Co-administration of photosensitizing drugs may enhance phototoxic reactions during photodynamic therapy with aminolevulinic acid. 7. Demeclocycline reduces the effects of amoxicillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Tetracyclines may interfere with the bactericidal action of penicillins. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of penicillins when used concomitantly with tetracyclines. 8. Demeclocycline reduces the effects of ampicillin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 9. Demeclocycline increases the effects of atracurium through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 10. Demeclocycline reduces the efficacy of the BCG vaccine (live) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 11. Bismuth subsalicylate decreases demeclocycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 12. Calcium acetate and demeclocycline reduce each other’s levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or separate administration by at least 2 hours. 13. Calcium carbonate, calcium chloride, calcium citrate, and calcium gluconate all interact similarly with demeclocycline, reducing each other’s levels by inhibiting GI absorption. These interactions apply only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or separate administration by at least 2 hours. 14. Carbonyl iron decreases demeclocycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 15. Demeclocycline reduces the efficacy of the cholera vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received systemic antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 16. Demeclocycline increases the effects of cisatracurium via pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 17. Demeclocycline reduces the effects of dicloxacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 18. Ferric maltol, ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, ferrous sulfate, iron dextran complex, and iron sucrose all decrease demeclocycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. These interactions apply only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 19. Isotretinoin and demeclocycline are contraindicated due to the risk of pseudotumor cerebri. 20. Magnesium chloride, magnesium citrate, magnesium hydroxide, magnesium oxide, and magnesium sulfate all decrease demeclocycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. These interactions apply only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Administer magnesium 2 hours before or 4 hours after demeclocycline to avoid chelation. 21. Methoxyflurane and demeclocycline increase each other’s toxicity via pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of nephrotoxicity. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 22. Methyl aminolevulinate and demeclocycline increase each other’s toxicity via pharmacodynamic synergy, enhancing photosensitizing effects. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 23. Demeclocycline reduces the effects of oral microbiota supplements by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Antibiotics may decrease the efficacy of bacterial spores in microbiota supplements. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating microbiota therapy. 24. Demeclocycline reduces the effects of nafcillin, oxacillin, and penicillin G/VK through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 25. Demeclocycline increases the effects of pancuronium, rapacuronium, rocuronium, succinylcholine, and vecuronium via pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 26. Rose hips decrease demeclocycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 27. Sodium bicarbonate and sodium citrate/citric acid decrease demeclocycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. These interactions apply only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or separate administration by at least 2 hours. 28. Strontium ranelate decreases demeclocycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This combination is contraindicated. Suspend strontium ranelate during antibiotic therapy. 29. Demeclocycline reduces the effects of temocillin and piperacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 30. Tretinoin (oral and topical) and demeclocycline increase each other’s phototoxicity via pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 31. Tripotassium dicitrato bismuthate decreases demeclocycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 32. Demeclocycline reduces the efficacy of live typhoid vaccines through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 33. Demeclocycline decreases the levels or effects of oral contraceptives (e.g., conjugated estrogens, estradiol, ethinyl estradiol, mestranol) by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 34. Lanthanum carbonate decreases demeclocycline levels by cation binding in the GI tract. Administer oral tetracyclines at least 2 hours before or after lanthanum. This interaction applies only to oral tetracyclines. 35. Magnesium supplements reduce demeclocycline levels by forming insoluble complexes that inhibit absorption. Administer magnesium 2 hours before or 4 hours after demeclocycline. 36. Demeclocycline increases methotrexate levels by decreasing its elimination. Use caution and monitor. Tetracyclines may interfere with methotrexate metabolism by inhibiting bowel flora. 37. Methoxsalen and demeclocycline increase each other’s phototoxicity via pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor. 38. Mipomersen and demeclocycline increase each other’s toxicity, potentially elevating hepatic enzymes. Monitor liver function tests (LFTs). 39. Polycarbophil decreases demeclocycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 40. Porfimer and demeclocycline enhance each other’s phototoxicity via pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor.
